When there's no internet — floods, cyclones, shutdowns — nearby amend phones pass messages and SOS alerts to each other over Bluetooth and Wi-Fi Direct, hop by hop, until they reach your friend or a phone that's online, which uploads them. Messages stay end-to-end encrypted: phones that carry them can't read them, and your amend ID is never broadcast. Uses some extra battery while on.

amend has no accounts, no ads and no analytics. This is what happens with your data:
Your identity is a key created on this phone and stored in Android's secure storage. We never see it. If you lose it without a backup, nobody can recover it.

Encrypted on your phone before they leave it (NIP-17/44 for messages, DTLS-SRTP for calls, AES-256-GCM for voice and video). Relays and file servers only see unreadable data, plus the recipient's public key and an approximate time.
Your profile (name, about, photo) and anything you post on the community eco map (photo, place, note). Photos are stripped of hidden camera data before upload.
Used only when you ask: SOS (sent only to the people you chose), weather (rounded to about 1 km and sent to Open-Meteo), the eco map and the icon's sunrise time (on the phone).
Steps, walking reports, your forest, points and settings never leave the device.

Nostr relays (messages), Blossom file servers (encrypted media), Cloudflare TURN (relaying encrypted calls on strict networks), Open-Meteo (weather), OpenStreetMap (map tiles), Google STUN (finding a call path). Each sees your IP address, like any website.
Settings → Privacy & security → Remove identity deletes your key and all messages from this phone.
